items.title: Bivariant Chow cohomology of a scheme of finite type over a field with target the point is ordinary Chow homology in complementary degree
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts a canonical identification A^p(X -> Spec(k)) = CH_{-p}(X) for a scheme X locally of finite type over a field k and every p (statement lines 14182-14190). One direction is immediate from capping with the class of the point, but the converse must build a bivariant class out of an arbitrary cycle class alpha: writing alpha = sum n_i [X_i], the author forms the proper map g from the disjoint union of the X_i to X and the flat map f from that disjoint union to Spec(k) of relative dimension -p, multiplies by the integer n_i through a bivariant class nu on the disjoint union, and obtains the required class as g_* o nu o f^*, using that flat pullback and proper pushforward are bivariant operations (proof lines 14193-14224). The mutual inverses are then checked by reducing, through the bivariant-class axiom for the empty class, to integral X' for which the structure morphism is flat of relative dimension dim(X'), so that [X'] = (p')^*[Spec(k)] (proof lines 14227-14240). The construction of the converse class rather than the identification itself is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
